name: Risk Management
description: Identification, measurement, monitoring, and mitigation of financial and non-financial risks across the bank

sub_capabilities.name: Credit Risk
sub_capabilities.description: Counterparty creditworthiness assessment, exposure monitoring across portfolios, expected credit loss provisioning, and limit management in line with IFRS 9 and Basel IRB requirements

sub_capabilities.name: Market Risk
sub_capabilities.description: Measurement and management of trading book risk, interest rate risk in the banking book (IRRBB), FX exposure, and Value-at-Risk reporting under the Fundamental Review of the Trading Book (FRTB)

sub_capabilities.name: Operational Risk
sub_capabilities.description: Incident identification and management, internal loss data collection, risk and control self-assessments (RCSAs), scenario analysis, and capital modelling under the Basel Standardised Measurement Approach

sub_capabilities.name: Fraud Detection
sub_capabilities.description: Real-time and batch transaction monitoring for fraudulent activity, management of fraud rule engines, first-party and third-party fraud case management, and liaison with law enforcement and card scheme fraud networks

promotion_test.promotion_rationale: Distinct external participants (Action Fraud, NCA, card schemes, law enforcement); governed by a separate regulatory framework (Fraud Act 2006, PSR fraud reimbursement rules, PSR APP fraud mandatory reimbursement 2024); operates an independent investigate-detect-report-recover lifecycle not shared with prudential risk; requires independent scalability driven by transaction volume spikes and scheme rule changes orthogonal to risk capital cycles

sub_capabilities.name: Model Risk
sub_capabilities.description: Independent validation of internal rating, pricing, and stress-testing models, backtesting of model outputs, model inventory governance, and PRA model risk management expectations compliance

design_decisions.title: Fraud Detection promoted to standalone capability
design_decisions.decision: CAP-004.04 Fraud Detection is elevated to an independent capability rather than remaining a sub-capability of Risk Management
design_decisions.rationale: Fraud detection involves a materially different participant ecosystem (law enforcement, Action Fraud, card scheme networks), operates under the Fraud Act 2006 and PSR mandatory APP reimbursement framework rather than the PRA prudential rulebook, follows a detect-investigate-recover lifecycle distinct from the risk capital measurement lifecycle, and must scale independently to absorb transaction volume peaks and rapid rule-change cycles without coupling to prudential risk processes
design_decisions.consequences: A dedicated Fraud capability domain will be defined. Interfaces between Fraud Detection and Operational Risk (loss data sharing) and Payments (transaction interception) must be formally specified as integration contracts

design_decisions.title: Credit, Market, and Operational Risk co-located within Risk Management
design_decisions.decision: The three core prudential risk sub-capabilities (Credit, Market, Operational) are retained within CAP-004 Risk Management rather than promoted
design_decisions.rationale: All three share the PRA/Basel regulatory reporting spine, feed the same Internal Capital Adequacy Assessment Process (ICAAP), are governed by the same Chief Risk Officer accountability, and rely on overlapping data sets (exposure data, P&L attribution). Promoting them would fracture the ICAAP aggregation surface without a corresponding reduction in coupling
design_decisions.consequences: A unified risk data platform serving all three sub-capabilities should be treated as shared infrastructure. Model Risk (CAP-004.05) acts as an independent second-line control over models used across all three sub-capabilities
